synthesis.headline: Only 4% of 100 testers would act, and high-skepticism users (33% of sample) average -0.84 sentiment because the 4.8% APY lacks a written guarantee and the FDIC pass-through mechanism is unexplained.

findings.claim: The FDIC pass-through coverage mechanism is not explained, causing universal confusion about how balances exceed $250k protection.
The 4.8% APY carries no written guarantee against rate drops, so high-skepticism users treat it as a teaser.
The dynamic yield optimization / allocation engine logic is undisclosed, leaving even tech-comfortable users unable to verify daily rate arbitrage.

highest_leverage_edit.current_text: No teaser rate that drops after 90 days.
highest_leverage_edit.proposed_text: APY guaranteed ≥ 4.5% for 12 months, backed by third-party audit — no teaser drop.
highest_leverage_edit.rationale: High-skepticism users explicitly demand a written, audited APY floor; the current 'no teaser' claim is unverified and dismissed.

synthesis.who_you_are_losing: High-skepticism users (skepticism ≥ 70, 33% of sample) and low-tech-comfort users (tech_comfort ≤ 30, 28% of sample) — together 55% of traffic — average -0.84 and -0.93 sentiment because they see no audited APY guarantee and no plain-language FDIC explanation.
synthesis.who_you_are_winning: High-tech-comfort, low-skepticism users (tech_comfort ≥ 75, skepticism ≤ 40, ~18% of sample) — the only segment with positive sentiment (+0.22) and all 4 converters come from this group.
